newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ailing Yeltsin should resign, says Gorbachev.
newsitem.headline: Ailing Yeltsin should resign, says Gorbachev.

text.p: Mikhail Gorbachev, the last president of the Soviet Union, called on Russian leader Boris Yeltsin to resign in a radio interview on Wednesday.
"The way things are going, the president (Yeltsin) must resign," Gorbachev said of his old political sparring partner in an interview with Ekho Moskvy radio.
Gorbachev was the architect of the "perestroika" and "glasnost" reforms from 1985 until 1991 when the Soviet Union collapsed and when Yeltsin became leader of a newly independent Russia.
He made the comments just before a group of prominent cardiologists in Moscow announced their decision that Yeltsin should undergo heart surgery within six or eight weeks.

Yeltsin, 65, has been in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital since September 13 where, aides have said, doctors are conducting tests and preparing him for a bypass operation to improve blood supply to the heart.

The Kremlin says Yeltsin is in full control of affairs of state. But his prolonged hospital stay has prompted demands from the Communist opposition that he should step down. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said this week that resignation was out of the question.
Yeltsin dropped out of the public eye in late June, just before he won another term in the Kremlin on July 3.
Gorbachev said Russia could not be "left a hostage of unclear, troubled times".

Recalling the Soviet Union's period of so-called "stagnation" under ailing Communist Party bosses in the 1970s and early 1980s, Gorbachev said former Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev's long period of illness had "stopped all work...At least 10 years were lost".
Gorbachev was one of several candidates who ran against Yeltsin but he won less than one per cent of the vote in the first round.
